newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New petrol retailer tipped for New Zealand - paper.
newsitem.headline: New petrol retailer tipped for New Zealand - paper.

text.p: New Zealand is expected to have another entrant to the petrol retailing market in competition with the so called "big four," the New Zealand Herald reported on Wednesday.
The paper said a mystery company was believed to have bought up to 30 prime sites around the country for stations in a move that could potentially lead to cheaper prices at the pump.
The Herald said the big four - Mobil Corp, British Petroleum Co Plc, Shell and Caltex were watching developments closely.
Real estate agents and property developers told the newspaper they believed the mystery player was Fletcher Energy, which has in the past expressed an interest in petrol retailing.
FCL Energy spokesmen were not immediately available for comment.
The paper quoted Energy Minister Max Bradford as saying he would welcome a new entrant.
"Over the last two or three months I have been observing the apparent increase in the margins," he said.
This had been disputed by some oil companies, he said, but a new operator would "prove or disprove very quickly whether there is in fact plenty of competition".
Bradford said earlier this year that if the oil companies were fattening their margins, the government would encourage new entrants.
Bradford favours supermarket chains selling petrol, as is the case in Britain, France and Japan.
About 60 percent of petrol stations in New Zealand are owned by the big four and most of the rest are under contract to them.
FCL Energy recently bought a terminal in Brisbane to store oil and may have done the same in New Zealand, the paper said.
The company produces about 11 million barrels of oil a year from its New Zealand fields.
